Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Arjun Patel (Redwood PM), Carlos Mendez (Lighthouse CISO), Priya Kapoor (Lighthouse Platform Eng), Ellen Lowe (CTO), Samir Rao (DevOps)

Optional auto sections (auto-gen may be messy):
Summary: High-level walkthrough of SAML/SCIM setup patterns and how Redwood supports least-privilege RBAC. Touched on KMS integration for encryption at rest, audit logging retention, and data residency options. Agreed on pilot timeline and deliverables.
Topics: SAML bindings, SP-initiated flows, SCIM mapping for groups, RBAC role mapping, KMS customer keys, audit log format and retention, on-prem/private deployment notes.
Action items: see metadata field for structured action items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: All right, good afternoon everyone, uh good morning for some of you. This is Jordan from Redwood, thanks for carving out the time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Carlos: Hey this is Carlos, CISO, Lighthouse.
[00:08] Priya: Priya here. Platform eng.
[00:09] Ellen: Ellen, CTO.
[00:10] Samir: Samir, DevOps.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Maya and Arjun from my side too; Maya you'll take the bulk of the deep dive.
[00:16] Maya: Hey all. I'll start with a quick framing then we can jump into the SAML/SCIM specifics and then the RBAC model.

[02:05] Maya: So high level, Redwood supports both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML. We commonly recommend SP-initiated for user flows into the Console to avoid unnecessary IdP redirects on system calls, but for automated provisioning SCIM/token-based flows are, uh, more predictable.
[02:28] Priya: Quick question — we run Okta and Azure AD in parallel for different orgs. Any gotchas?
[02:33] Maya: Yes. Dual-IdP setups are supported. You can map IdPs to groups or org units with our SCIM group sync. The main gotcha is consistent email or immutable user id across both, otherwise you'll end up with duplicate accounts. The transcription often says e-mail as a mutable key; we strongly recommend using the federated id (NameID) as the canonical key.

[04:15] Carlos: For audit and compliance, we need immutable proof of who did what — can Redwood's audit logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
[04:24] Arjun: Yep, we support forwarding via syslog/HTTPS webhook or direct S3 export. Logs include token-level metadata, model id, route, and redwood-user id. There's a small caveat: PII in payloads is truncated at collection points but you'll see request/response hashes and token counts.
[04:47] Ellen: Is the request content hashed or is there any chance of payload being stored in plaintext in logs?
[04:53] Maya: By default we redact full-input in audit telemetry; retention is configurable. For Private deployments you can choose to keep logs in your VPC S3 and disable any control-plane copies.

[06:30] Samir: For KMS — we use AWS KMS with multi-region keys. How does Redwood integrate, especially if we go Private?
[06:38] Maya: With Private, we offer KMS integration patterns: customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) via IAM roles and key policies, or we can use envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys. For BYOK you give us an IAM role with decrypt permissions; nothing leaves your KMS unencrypted. There was a small transcript glitch earlier where someone said 'KMS as KMS' — yes it's KMS.

[08:20] Carlos: We need to ensure key rotation policies and split access; can't have our ops team rotate and still break service. Thoughts?
[08:28] Arjun: We support key aliasing and automatic rotation. We recommend a staging alias that points to the active key; rotation is done by rotating the alias. The service uses the alias so rotation doesn't break ciphertext references. We also support a policy where Redwood never has Decrypt unless explicitly granted and that can be audited in CloudTrail.

[10:12] Priya: SCIM — our current schema has nested groups and teams, 10k users. How does Redwood handle SCIM rate limits and bulk provisioning?
[10:23] Maya: We support incremental SCIM syncs by group and delta tokens. For initial bulk imports we recommend a CSV push into the Console or a one-time bulk SCIM endpoint where you can batch 500 users per call. For 10k we usually do a phased import with group-based syncs to avoid throttling. Also note some IdPs (cough, older AAD) will return inconsistent group ids which is painful — we recommend canonicalizing groups on your IdP side when possible.

[12:41] Carlos: On RBAC — we want least privilege. Our concern is the number of roles multiplying across models/environments. How do customers map roles?
[12:51] Maya: Two patterns we've seen. First, role templates: admin/devops/engineer/readonly mapped to resource-scoped permissions (model:invoke, model:upload, console:user-mgmt). Second, permission bundles per application environment — e.g., staging vs prod has separate role IDs. We recommend group-based binding via SCIM so you don't need per-user assignments.

[14:33] Priya: Example — our data science team needs model inference access but not key rotation or billing. How to set that?
[14:40] Maya: Create a 'ds-infer' role with model:invoke and embeddings:read and map SCIM group DS to that role. Deny billing and kms:admin. You can also set session-level constraints like max tokens per call or rate-limit per API key.

[16:05] Ellen: Is there support for time-bound elevated privileges? E.g., someone needs admin for 2 hours for troubleshooting.
[16:12] Arjun: Yes, we have temporary role elevation flows integrated with SSO. You can request an admin elevation which creates a short-lived token; the action is logged and can require approval via your IdP if you chain it with an approval app.

[18:02] Carlos: For SOC 2 evidence — what artifacts do you provide?
[18:08] Jordan: We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA, ISO cert snapshots, and our control matrix. We'll include audit log extracts and the RBAC mappings used during the pilot for evidence.

[19:30] Priya: Data residency — our EU clinical operations require EU-only storage for certain datasets. How granular is your residency control?
[19:39] Maya: On Hosted, you can pin workloads to region-specific clusters; Private gives you full control. For hybrid setups you can configure per-route residency; e.g., any request with a tag 'eu-pii' routes to EU-only capacity. There's a small note: model weights sometimes need to be pulled for certain hosted optimizations; we ensure those operations are also region-restricted for pinned workloads.

[21:10] Samir: Are there any latency or cost trade-offs when we force EU-only?
[21:16] Arjun: Slightly higher costs due to regional capacity differences and reduced pooling, and sometimes higher cold-start times for models not prewarmed in that region. But predictable locality is the trade.

[23:00] Carlos: On integrations — we use Hashicorp Vault for secrets. Can Redwood pull wrapping keys or integrate with Vault transit?
[23:10] Maya: For Private, yes. We can integrate with Vault transit for envelope keys and use Vault's sign/verify for token signing. For Hosted, we have a connector pattern that can proxy requests to your Vault in your VPC. Implementation details depend on whether we have network peering.

[25:40] Priya: How are service accounts handled? We have machine identities for pipelines.
[25:47] Maya: Service accounts are created as non-human identities in SCIM with a specific naming convention; we recommend using rotating secrets or short-lived tokens and binding to roles. We support OAuth2 client credentials for machine-to-machine flows.

[28:05] Samir: Can we sync our existing role matrix CSV? We have hundreds of groups.
[28:12] Jordan: Yes, send the CSV. We'll prototype a mapping. Maya will produce a suggested mapping and Arjun will look at potential complexity for private vs hosted.

[30:00] Maya: Quick demo snippet — (screen share described) console > access > SSO settings. You paste IdP metadata, map NameID to federated id, choose SCIM group path, and preview sample mappings. In the demo there was a small glitch in the transcription where 'NameID' came out as 'Name one D' — ignore that.

[32:10] Priya: About SCIM group attribute mapping — do you support custom attributes for team-owner or environment tags?
[32:18] Maya: Yes, we support custom scim:extension attributes and you can map those to role tags. Those tags can be used in routing/policy rules, too.

[34:00] Carlos: For long-term retention, do you support immutable logs or WORM? We may need that for audits.
[34:08] Arjun: If you keep logs in your S3 under Private deployment, you can enable S3 Object Lock / WORM and lifecycle policies. On Hosted, we provide exports to your S3 where you control retention; Redwood doesn't enforce deletion inside customer-owned buckets.

[36:30] Ellen: OK, curious about emergency access. If we revoke a key, how fast do tokens get invalidated?
[36:38] Maya: Token revocation depends on TTL. Live API keys can be revoked immediately; for long-lived session tokens there's a revocation table we check on token validation which is near real-time (sub-60 seconds). In some extreme caching cases you may have up to a minute of grace.

[38:50] Priya: Can we limit model uploads to a subset of users? Because models contain trained IP.
[38:58] Maya: Absolutely. model:upload permission can be scoped to org or team. We also support checksum validation and optional automated malware scans on upload.

[40:20] Jordan: Competitors question — you mentioned LargeCloudAI and VertexServe. Where are they weak?
[40:28] Carlos: They either lock you into a single region or don't give private KMS integration, which is our main worry.
[40:34] Jordan: Understood. That's where Private or Dedicated helps.

[42:00] Maya: One more note on RBAC mapping: avoid per-model per-user roles. Use role templates + resource tags + group bindings. That keeps the role count manageable.

[44:10] Samir: Is there an API to automate role creation during our CI/CD deployments?
[44:16] Maya: Yes, full admin APIs: create-role, bind-group, set-policy. We recommend doing it through infrastructure-as-code templates we provide.

[46:05] Priya: Regarding encryption, does Redwood ever have access to plaintext model inputs in the control plane?
[46:12] Arjun: Not in Private. In Hosted, telemetry may include abstracted input metrics but full input is redacted. If you need zero plaintext exposure, Private is the recommended path. We'll also provide DLP patterns if you want to scrub PII before traffic reaches the service.

[48:30] Carlos: We have a compliance auditor who will want to test account provisioning and RBAC. Can we get a test tenant?
[48:36] Jordan: Yes. We'll spin up a sandbox tenant scoped to your pilot that mimics your planned tenancy and share credentials and a test script for the auditor.

[50:10] Priya: For the pilot, we want SCIM group sync, KMS BYOK, and an RBAC mapping for Prod+Staging — is that achievable in 2 weeks?
[50:18] Jordan: Yes, if we get IdP metadata and role matrix this week. Maya, Arjun — any blockers?
[50:24] Maya: None on engineering side. We'll need the IdP cert and test user.
[50:28] Arjun: We'll also need network details if you want a Private/Tunneled setup.

[52:00] Jordan: Quick recap — next steps: Jordan will share SOC2/ISO artifacts and the SAML/SCIM integration doc; Maya will deliver RBAC mapping suggestion; Lighthouse to provide IdP metadata and role matrix; we'll schedule pilot kickoff for week of 3/23.

[53:10] Carlos: Sounds good. I may ask for a short checklist for our security team to review beforehand.
[53:16] Jordan: We'll do that — checklist + demo recording + a short playbook for the auditor.

[54:40] Ellen: One last question — are there any known limitations for HIPAA workloads?
[54:47] Maya: We support HIPAA with Private deployments and BAAs (business associate agreements). The main constraint is ensuring PHI never leaves your controlled regions and appropriate logging/consent flows are in place. We'll send the BAAs sample.

[56:20] Carlos: OK thanks everyone.
[56:23] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and the timeline.
[56:28] Priya: Thanks.
[56:29] Maya: Bye all.

[56:45] (call ends)
